text:
maria_support: Hey team, customer reported a CSV export that downloads but is truncated in the middle of a row. file size ~1.2MB but Excel shows last row cut off and comma counts mismatch. customer = ACME corp.

maria_support: repro steps from customer: Console -> Analytics -> Export CSV (custom date range) -> download. Happens intermittently (~1/20 exports). They saw emojis and non-ascii chars in event metadata.

sam_eng: thanks, can you paste the exact payload they used? also which model of export (async job vs direct stream)?

maria_support: they used the UI export (async job) not the streaming endpoint. I requested the job id, they sent job_id: job_2026_03_14_90.

kyle_analytics: I'm seeing a couple of similar S3 objects from that timeframe with size mismatch logs. Could be our streaming gzipping layer + content-length mismatch.

maria_support: attaching the customer's report snippet and the bytes observed in Excel: "user_id,session_id,event,props\n123,abc,click,\"hello\uD83D\uDE03\"\n456,def,pageview,\"/pricing,plan=pro\"\n789,ghi,submit,partial_row" - they saw the last line truncated to "partial_"

sam_eng: can you share the export service logs for job_2026_03_14_90? a quick check: when we gzip+stream we must not set Content-Length. If downstream S3 presigned PUT expects length maybe client aborted mid-upload.

export-bot: [export-service] job job_2026_03_14_90 status=completed uploaded=1 object=s3://redwood-exports/prod/2026/03/job_2026_03_14_90.csv.gz size=1240973

kyle_analytics: the object exists but I see an early EOF in the object at byte 1240210 (≈-763 bytes). Our logs show a 499/connection reset at the same second from export-worker-7.

ria_sre: 499 suggests client closed connection before finishing upload. Could be client UI cancelling if user navigates away, or intermediate LB timing out. What's our LB idle timeout for uploads?

sam_eng: LB timeout is 60s for HTTP/1.1. But the job uploads via presigned PUT directly to S3 from worker, so LB shouldn't matter. Need to check if worker code streams through a buffer and then PUTs; if it streams a gzipped stream into PUT multipart we might be incorrectly assuming size and then aborting.

maria_support: customer reported this happens more with larger ranges and when there are emojis / multibyte chars. They also tried reopening file in VSCode and saw garbled bytes near EOF.

sam_eng: emojis increase byte count vs char count; if we compute Content-Length by chars, that's a bug. Can you paste the worker upload snippet?

maria_support: they shared a stack trace from their side (UI): "GET /exports/job_2026_03_14_90/download -> 200, then browser aborted with net::ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING"

sam_eng: aha, browser reported ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING when client streaming response from our backend. That indicates our API returned a Transfer-Encoding: chunked response but closed mid-stream (server-side). Could be an unhandled exception in the worker while serializing last rows (e.g., UnicodeEncodeError) or OOM. Check worker logs around exception.

kyle_analytics: query: show me last 20 log lines for worker job_2026_03_14_90.

export-bot: [export-worker-7] 2026-03-14T21:03:12Z INFO starting job job_2026_03_14_90
export-bot: [export-worker-7] 2026-03-14T21:03:14Z INFO stream rows -> gzipping
export-bot: [export-worker-7] 2026-03-14T21:03:58Z WARN s3 upload retry=1 cause=EPIPE
export-bot: [export-worker-7] 2026-03-14T21:03:59Z ERROR upload failed: Broken pipe
export-bot: [export-worker-7] 2026-03-14T21:04:00Z INFO aborting job, marking completed_with_warnings

ria_sre: Broken pipe while writing to S3 could be from SDK treating stream incorrectly or connection reset by S3; but we also saw the browser error which suggests our API streamed to browser and then attempted a separate S3 upload? Clarify architecture: do we stream directly to browser while also uploading to S3, or do we generate to S3 and then provide download link?

sam_eng: current flow: worker streams CSV -> gzip -> tee to S3 upload + buffer to response store. For UI async job we PUT to S3 (presigned) and then store metadata. If S3 PUT fails mid-way we still mark job completed because of a race in the state machine (bug). That explains truncated object.

maria_support: so root cause hypothesis: downstream EPIPE during S3 upload -> worker aborts and marks job completed -> UI presents download link that points to partial object -> user downloads truncated file / browser shows chunked encoding error.

sam_eng: fix plan: 1) hotfix to change state machine to mark job failed on upload failures (patch to exported job finalizer) 2) add multipart ETag/size verification after upload and retry on mismatch 3) instrument retry/backoff on EPIPE and increase S3 client timeouts 4) add content-size checksum in metadata and validate before marking completed.

kyle_analytics: also add telemetry to surface events with non-utf8 bytes and truncated_row=true in logs so support can detect quicker.

ria_sre: short-term mitigation: roll out hotfix to ensure we don't return download link when upload failed or partially uploaded. Also add a scheduler job to sweep recent exports and check object size vs expected; mark and re-run if mismatch.

sam_eng: @kyle_analytics can you add a Grafana alert for export failures and objects with size < expected by >1KB?

kyle_analytics: on it. Will add alert with runbook linking to this thread.

maria_support: customer-facing message draft: "We're investigating an intermittent issue where some Analytics CSV exports may be truncated when the export contains large or multibyte characters. We've implemented a temporary block to prevent partial downloads and are deploying a fix to ensure uploads are retried or marked failed. We'll follow up when fully resolved." ok to send?

sam_eng: ok to send. Add ask for job ids if they see future occurrences.

maria_support: sending to customer now. I'll update thread if they provide more. Thanks all :pray:

ria_sre: follow-up tasks for eng: - PR to finalizer logic (fail on upload errors) - add post-upload size verification - increase s3 client timeouts and retry config - add sweep job to requeue bad exports

sam_eng: I'll open an internal ticket and link to this thread, assign to export-service squad. ETA for hotfix: 24h. Full fix: 3-5 days.

maria_support: marking as escalated. If anyone gets more repros @maria_support. :thumbsup:
